design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 of damage_claims_and_protection (category protect). Round 2 (rework after the policy-task audit).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A San Diego host asks one thing: accept the settlement on her approved jewelry (valuables) claim. Getting the number right forces the adjuster workflow of HostCover: find the plan and both claims of the August stay, notice from the valuables rule's prerequisite sentence that the stay's approved theft claim must first carry its reimbursement, settle that theft claim (six factors, one of them read from her 2025 theft history), and only then settle the valuables claim on the changed ledger (six factors, the deductible input moved by the theft write). The difficulty is reading rules and records and calculating; there is one obvious tool per problem.

2. SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): key env_0045_vacation_rental_platform/damage_claims_and_protection/0, prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6, 6]; theft and valuables take 6 each. Claimed: protect_ext_theft_settlement (pay_theft_reimbursement_c380c173, agent), protect_ext_valuables_settlement (accept_valuables_settlement_01cb0de3, user). Task 1 holds property, pet and income loss. Declared deviation (kept): reimbursement rows carry the base event's payout trigger; the payout desk books the credit, no task tool writes a payout table.

3. POLICIES, LINEAGE, TRIGGERS. Both refine protect_evt_reimbursement (subject protect_reimbursement_paid) and list protect_agg_plan_year_limits. Theft: state_due. Valuables: on_request (booked only when the host accepts it in person, because the value of art, jewellery and collectibles rests on her own appraisals and receipts). Declared overwrites: the order clause (shares come after depreciation and give the adjusted loss), 'subtract every guest payment recorded on the claim (net of reversals)' (replaced by the recovery-sharing method), 'subtract deductible_usd' (per-stay deductible share), and for valuables the depreciation schedule (a gentler valuables schedule). Everything else of base is inherited.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root protect_ext_valuables_settlement; prerequisite protect_ext_theft_settlement; edge valuables -> theft, value_input, gate va_stay_settled, form state; sentence 'Where the same stay also carries an approved theft claim, the valuables settlement is fixed only after the plan's HostCover ledger shows a reimbursement on that theft claim.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after' (affirmative; negated form 'not fixed until ...' adds and drops nothing); the waited-on side is a record-visible ledger state; no tool, id or code token; scope = the approved theft claim of the same stay. Exactly one write books a reimbursement on a theft claim (pay_theft_reimbursement_c380c173). False at the opening: the August theft claim dd2413c0-fcc5-4c1d-b037-0760ad41c3c6 is approved and its only ledger rows are a request and a 40.00 guest payment (the plan's only reimbursement is on the 2025 claim of another stay). Owner of the root: the customer (accept_valuables_settlement_01cb0de3). Order theft -> valuables. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping the theft write gives valuables 771.40 instead of 832.20. user_scenario names no prerequisite; tools validate nothing.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. claim_approved: both claims approved 2026-10-02. escalated_in_time: deadlines 2026-09-03, escalations 2026-09-23 (day 20; last standing day 2026-10-03, a 2026-10-04 escalation fails). one_reimbursement_per_claim: no reimbursement on either August claim. protect_agg_plan_year_limits: policy_scope; nothing paid since the 2026-05-10 plan-year start. Coverage: check-in 2026-08-24 under Plus (changed 2026-01-20), plan active.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Plan e73e0f06-1797-4f82-bd62-532796d64140; August stay ad36097a-b8a0-4079-aef8-da6069b35316; theft claim dd2413c0-fcc5-4c1d-b037-0760ad41c3c6 (verified 1870.00, 41 months), valuables claim e5df89df-3645-425f-b517-c9e99e94d164 (verified 3400.00, 88 months); guest payments 40.00 / 25.00 each on its own claim. Earlier history: spring 2025 stay 726daa3b-4dd7-45c0-9025-b5154509931a (guest Daniel Okafor), theft claim f07a94ae-2a97-4be5-ae40-fce571907b22 approved 2025-04-17 and reimbursed 565.00 on 2025-04-22. Included per computation: each claim's own row and payment; for the theft repeat-loss share the approved theft claims of other stays in 24 months; for the deductible factors the reimbursements of other stays in 12 months. Excluded: requests and premiums (not guest payments), the other claim's payment, the August claim itself in the repeat count.

7. FACTOR CARD (actual run). Theft (expected 620.46; all-baseline 1705.00): depreciation 41 months -> 40 percent (baseline 1098.72); access Private Room -> 75 percent (cross listing; baseline 859.42; an insurance analogue: theft by persons with lawful access to shared quarters); deductible factor Superhost run from 2026-07-01 AND no other-stay reimbursement in 12 months -> 0.5 (multi-source, cross host; baseline 561.43; near-misses: the 2026-04-01 demotion, the 2025-04-22 reimbursement just outside 12 months); recovery-sharing method HostCover Plus -> proportional sharing (baseline insurer-first 616.98); repeat-loss one approved theft claim from another stay in 24 months -> 90 percent (baseline 700.05; near-miss: the August claim itself); escalation 20 days -> 95 percent (baseline 658.15). Valuables (expected 832.20; all-baseline 2500.00): depreciation 88 months -> 20 percent (baseline 1061.36); access Private Room -> 50 percent (baseline 1749.35); new-cover 216 days -> 75 percent (cross host; baseline 1137.78); escalation 20 days -> 90 percent (baseline 934.03); deductible factor 0.5 (multi-source; the step-13 reimbursement is on the same stay and left out; baseline 771.40); recovery-sharing proportional (baseline 830.50).

8. THE RECOVERY-SHARING METHOD (replaces the round-1 guest-payment ladder). Three allocation rules used in property claims for money recovered from the person responsible: the insured is made whole first (only the larger of the guest payments and the deductible is subtracted), proportional sharing (the deductible plus the guest payments times the adjusted loss less the deductible, divided by the adjusted loss), and the insurer credited first (payments and deductible both subtracted). The tier follows the HostCover level: Premier, Elite and Estate make the host whole first; Standard and Plus share proportionally; Essential, the free level, credits Roamhaven first, which is also the baseline the computation document states. Each tier selects a different figure whenever a guest payment stands (here, theft: 620.46 proportional vs 656.98 made-whole-first vs 616.98 insurer-first).

9. WORLD ROWS AND WHY. customers: host, August guest, 2025 guest (government_id_last4 5367, 5701, 5144, all 5000-5799). listings: Private Room (access shares). host_accounts: Superhost since 2026-07-01. host_account_events: fees assessed at both check-ins and four Superhost assessments. payout_methods: default ACH. stays: the spring 2025 stay and the August 2026 stay. protection_plans: Plus since 2026-01-20 (Standard before). protection_claims: the two August claims and the 2025 theft claim. protection_events: premiums on both stays, three requests, two partial guest payments, the 2025 reimbursement. Every row is read by a gold read (closure check): stays through find_stays by host account, the two guests through find_stays by guest.

10. PERSONA DESIGN. Marisol (warm, chatty retired librarian) volunteers only the jewelry settlement request; gives phone 6195835412 and licence last four 5367 when asked; identifies the claim by the August 29 check-out and August 31 filing; mentions the laptop and speaker only if asked what else was taken and the 2025 tablet claim only if asked whether this happened before; agrees to whatever must be booked first; questions the figure once and accepts the answer; runs the acceptance with exactly the agent's values; keeps her account; closes on booking.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read plan, claims, ledger, stays (by host account, by each guest), listing, host account and records, payout methods. Valuables rule -> its prerequisite sentence -> the August theft claim is unreimbursed -> theft: 1870.00 x 0.60 x 0.75 x 0.90 x 0.95 = 719.4825; deductible 250/2 x 0.5 = 62.50; proportional offset 62.50 + 40.00 x 656.9825 / 719.4825 = 99.0253 -> 620.46 with pay_theft_reimbursement_c380c173. Valuables: 3400.00 x 0.80 x 0.50 x 0.75 x 0.90 = 918.00; deductible 250 x 1/2 x 0.5 = 62.50; offset 62.50 + 25.00 x 855.50 / 918.00 = 85.7979 -> 832.20, handed over with accept_valuables_settlement_01cb0de3.

12. VERIFICATION. A temporary authoring script (removed at the end of the run, as instructed) replayed the gold writes to each handling time with check_compute's evaluator: theft 620.46 (factor baselines 1098.72 / 859.42 / 561.43 / 616.98 / 700.05 / 658.15, all 1705.00); valuables 832.20 (1061.36 / 1749.35 / 1137.78 / 934.03 / 771.40 / 830.50, all 2500.00); edge skipped 771.40. No declared figure sits on a half-cent tie. check_compute --task 0 reproduces them.

13. CLOSURE. theft -> pay_theft_reimbursement_c380c173 -> computations[0] (step 13, 620.46); valuables -> accept_valuables_settlement_01cb0de3 -> computations[1] (step 15, 832.20). charter_scope = required_documents; tools in first-call order. Negative space: no new guest request, no denial, no payout change.

14. SOLVABILITY AGAINST GT AND DRAFT RECOMPUTATION. Each call cites the approved claim row, the deadline/escalation fields with frozen_time and the request row for the dedup, bound to claim_id. From the published rules, schemas, finder returns and persona alone the same objects, order and amounts follow; the 2025 reimbursement is excluded from the 12-month count by its date and the August claim from the repeat count by 'leaving out claims on the same stay'.

15. REVISIONS. r1/r2 (round 1): claim lookup inlined into the tools; closure-driven removal of history. Round 2 (audit items): F-G1 - the guest-payment ladder had only two distinct outcomes; replaced in both policies by the recovery-sharing method (three allocation rules keyed to the HostCover level). F-G2 - the theft documentation share keyed to the listing's marketing-photo count was removed; replaced by the theft repeat-loss share, backed by the seeded 2025 theft claim on another stay (plus its stay, guest, request, premium, reimbursement and fee rows, and two reads). O-L5 - 'agreed value' wording removed from the valuables rule and tool. O-T0-2 - every rule now says 'rounded half up to the nearest cent' and no declared figure is a tie. Figures moved: theft 656.98 -> 620.46, valuables 855.50 -> 832.20.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Ibarra, a retired middle-school librarian in San Diego who rents out the spare bedroom of her North Park house on Roamhaven under the title Sunny Garden Room near Balboa Park. You are warm and a little chatty, and you like to understand a step before you take it.

A guest who stayed with you at the end of August walked off with your late mother's gold watch and a pair of diamond stud earrings. You filed it with HostCover, and an email this week told you the claims team approved your jewelry claim (the email called it a valuables claim) and that you need to accept the valuables settlement to get paid. That is what you want today: to accept the valuables settlement and have the money come to you. You have not seen a figure yet and you have no idea how it is worked out.

You open with your name and say you are calling about the jewelry claim. When the agent asks how to find your profile, you give your mobile number, 6195835412. When the agent needs to confirm it is you, you give the last four of your driver's license, 5367; if asked for anything more you also know your email, marisol.ibarra@sdmail.net, and your date of birth, February 14, 1981. You do not know any claim or plan reference numbers; if asked which claim, you say the guest checked out on August 29 and you filed the jewelry claim on August 31. If the agent asks whether the guest took anything else, you say yes, your laptop and a small speaker from the living room, and that you filed for those as well. If the agent asks whether anything like this has happened before, you say yes, in spring 2025 another guest took a tablet and headphones and HostCover paid that claim.

If the agent tells you that something else on your HostCover plan has to be paid or booked before the jewelry settlement can be offered, you are glad to hear it and tell the agent to go ahead; you do not ask for the details. When the agent tells you the settlement amount, and it is far below the 3,650 dollars you put on the claim, you say gently that it is a lot less than you claimed and ask how they got there; whatever the agent explains, you accept it and you never suggest a number of your own. When the agent hands you the step to accept the settlement yourself, you use exactly the claim reference and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back what the confirmation says. You want the money to go to the usual bank account on file and you do not want to change anything about your payouts or your plan. Once the agent confirms the settlement has been accepted and booked, you thank them and say goodbye.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_id: Value dd2413c0-fcc5-4c1d-b037-0760ad41c3c6. Basis: the tool docstring defines claim_id as 'the reference number of the approved theft claim being reimbursed, as returned by the damage-claim lookup for the host's HostCover plan', and the theft rule 'settles a theft claim that the claims team has approved on a HostCover plan'. find_protection_claims (step 3) returns two approved theft claims: dd2413c0-fcc5-4c1d-b037-0760ad41c3c6 on the August stay with no reimbursement, and f07a94ae-2a97-4be5-ae40-fce571907b22 on the spring 2025 stay, already reimbursed 565.00 on 2025-04-22. Uniqueness: 'A claim is reimbursed once' excludes the 2025 claim; the valuables claim is another category.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 620.46. Verified theft loss 1870.00. Theft depreciation share: Plus depreciates items and the claim records the stolen items as 41 months old -> 37 to 60 tier, 40 percent, 1122.00. Theft access share: Private Room -> 75 percent, 841.50. Theft repeat-loss share: approved theft claims from other stays in the 24 months before 2026-10-07 = 1 (the 2025-04-17 claim; the August claim is on the same stay and left out) -> 90 percent, 757.35. Theft escalation share: 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-23 = 20 days -> 8 to 21 tier, 95 percent; adjusted theft loss 719.4825 (no rounding between steps). Deductible share: Plus deductible_usd 250.00 / 2 approved claims on the stay = 125.00; theft deductible factor: Superhost run from 2026-07-01, on or before the 2026-08-24 check-in, and no claim from another stay reimbursed in the 12 months before 2026-10-07 (the 2025-04-22 reimbursement is outside) -> 0.5, deductible 62.50. Theft recovery-sharing method: HostCover Plus -> proportional sharing: subtract 62.50 plus 40.00 x (719.4825 - 62.50) / 719.4825 = 36.5253, offset 99.0253 -> 620.4572. Caps: theft sublimit 10000.00, per-claim 100000.00, remaining aggregate 200000.00 (nothing posted since the 2026-05-10 plan-year start) -> no cut. Rounded half up to the cent: 620.46.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 832.20, evaluated after the theft reimbursement of step 13 is on the ledger. Verified valuables loss 3400.00. Valuables depreciation share: 88 months -> 61 to 120 tier, 20 percent, 2720.00. Valuables access share: Private Room -> 50 percent, 1360.00. edges.condition: protection_events carries a protect_reimbursement_paid row whose claim_id is the approved theft claim filed on the same stay as the valuables claim.
edges.policy_source: Where the same stay also carries an approved theft claim, the valuables settlement is fixed only after the plan's HostCover ledger shows a reimbursement on that theft claim.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The August stay carries an approved theft claim whose only ledger rows are its payment request and the guest's partial payment; the plan's only reimbursement row is on the spring 2025 theft claim of another stay, so the August stay counts 0 reimbursed claims of 2 and the valuables claim would bear the whole 250.00 deductible.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 books a protect_reimbursement_paid row on the August theft claim; the stay's reimbursed count becomes 1 of 2, the valuables claim bears 125.00 x 0.5 = 62.50 instead of 125.00, and the valuables settlement is 832.20 instead of 771.40.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single chain with one edge: the theft reimbursement is written first and the valuables settlement after it, as the valuables rule's prerequisite sentence states; the reverse order gives a different terminal state (valuables 771.40). The theft settlement reads no valuables record, so its value (620.46) is the same either way.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 13 and replaying the rest: the valuables settlement recomputes to 771.40 (the stay shows 0 of 2 claims reimbursed, so the valuables claim bears 250.00 x 0.5 = 125.00, and the proportional offset becomes 125.00 + 25.00 x (918.00 - 125.00) / 918.00) instead of 832.20; the terminal ledger also lacks the theft reimbursement row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to accept the valuables (jewelry) settlement. It never names the theft claim, its reimbursement or any step that must come first; the laptop and speaker are mentioned only if the agent asks whether anything else was taken (and the spring 2025 claim only if asked whether anything like this happened before), and the one conditional about 'something else on your HostCover plan' fires only after the agent says so, with the customer agreeing without asking for details.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py pay_theft_reimbursement_c380c173 and accept_valuables_settlement_01cb0de3 each look up the claim only to copy its plan, host, stay and verified loss onto the new ledger row, then call ctx.create unconditionally; neither checks approval, escalation, earlier reimbursements or another claim of the stay, and neither returns an error. Calling the valuables acceptance before the theft reimbursement writes the row just the same, with whatever amount is passed.
